candidates.name: Ulcerative Colitis
support_spans: worsening crampy abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea
diffuse tenderness without guarding or rigidity
elevated fecal calprotectin at 2006 µg/g
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease, specifically ulcerative colitis.

candidates.name: Crohn's Disease
support_spans: segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon
subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, mild crypt architectural distortion, and an acute inflammatory infiltrate
candidates.why: The patient's colonoscopy and biopsy results show segmental inflammation and architectural distortion, which can be seen in Crohn's disease.

candidates.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
support_spans: elevated C-reactive protein
elevated fecal calprotectin
candidates.why: The patient's elevated inflammatory markers suggest an underlying inflammatory process.

candidates.name: Microscopic Colitis
support_spans: normal-appearing mucosa in the ascending colon, transverse colon, and rectum
subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, mild crypt architectural distortion
candidates.why: The patient's biopsy results show subepithelial edema and hemorrhage, which can be seen in microscopic colitis.

candidates.name: Ulcerative Colitis
support_spans: colonoscopy revealed segmental erythema and ulceration

candidates.why: The patient's colonoscopy and biopsy results are decisive for diagnosing ulcerative colitis.

candidates.name: Crohn's Disease
support_spans: contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrated mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon
candidates.why: The patient's CT results show bowel wall thickening, which can be seen in Crohn's disease.
